denial_reason_plain: The insurer (via eviCore) decided the Signatera blood test is experimental and not medically necessary in this case, so it will not be paid for.
specific_criterion: EviCore Criteria for Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven Laboratory Testing (MOL.CU.117) — 0340U classified as Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven (EIU).
weakness: Signatera has FDA Breakthrough Device designation and growing peer-reviewed support; several payers and Medicare cover 0340U in defined contexts. A blanket EIU classification that ignores the specific cancer type, stage, and treatment context may not reflect current evidence.
supporting_documentation: Letter of medical necessity from the ordering physician
Oncology treatment records (diagnosis, type, stage, treatment history)
Peer-reviewed studies supporting Signatera clinical utility
NCCN or ASCO guidelines supporting MRD testing
Comparative coverage policies from Medicare or other insurers for 0340U
appeal_deadline_hint: You have up to one year (365 days) from June 22, 2026 to appeal. However, if you want a panel of reviewers (instead of just one doctor) to look at your case — which may give you a stronger review — you must send your written appeal within 30 days of this letter (by approximately July 22, 2026). Act quickly if you want the panel review.
